info.title: Roleplay Character Engine API
info.summary: One explicit API implemented by web, future native clients, workers and the MCP adapter.
info.description:
RCE-053 task 2. Generated by scripts/build-openapi.mjs from a single endpoint table; run with --check to prove this document still matches it.

Owner is always derived from the verified principal and never from a payload. Request payload owner_id is not authority.
A model refusal is NOT an HTTP error: it is a typed failed turn outcome carrying provider_refused.
There is no arbitrary raw-state write endpoint. Definition edits and proposed narrative actions are distinct operations.

revision.description: Present only for versioned resources. Never another owner's revision (API.md).

next_cursor.description: Opaque. Absent when has_more is false.

api-envelope.Page.description: A cursor and the flag cannot contradict each other in either direction: has_more false forbids next_cursor, and has_more true requires it. Without the second rule a client is told more data exists but given no way to ask for it.

api-envelope.PaginationParams.description: limit defaults to 20 and caps at 100 (API.md).

api-envelope.AsyncOperation.description: Returned by write endpoints whose work is not complete on response. Terminal states carry either a resource reference or an error, never both and never neither.

api-error.ErrorCode.description: Stable codes. FRESHNESS_UNAVAILABLE is the retryable dependency failure ADR-004 requires when required state or visibility cannot be reconstructed completely.

api-error.StatusMatrix.description: Not a validation schema — the normative code-to-status mapping from API.md, kept beside the codes so the two cannot drift. 400 MALFORMED_REQUEST; 401 UNAUTHENTICATED; 403 FORBIDDEN; 404 NOT_FOUND; 409 STALE_REVISION, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, STATE_CONFLICT; 413 PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE; 422 SCHEMA_REJECTED, DOMAIN_REJECTED; 428 PRECONDITION_REQUIRED; 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED; 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE, FRESHNESS_UNAVAILABLE. A model refusal is NOT an HTTP error: it is a typed failed turn outcome with code provider_refused.

api-error.title: ApiError
api-error.description: The single error shape for every /v1 endpoint, per API.md. RCE-053. details carries safe field and constraint diagnostics only — never stack traces, never secret canonical facts, never another owner's revision.

character-core.title: CharacterCore
character-core.description: Creator-owned, global, mutable draft. RCE-003. Holds the working draft and pointers to published releases; a core edit never mutates a release or an existing scenario (INV-009). Holds the editable draft (character-draft) that GET/PATCH /v1/characters/{id} operates on. Unlike a release, a draft may carry an unknown age and half-authored fields — it simply cannot be published until it satisfies character-release, where the adult-age rule bites (INV-032).

current_release_id.description: Absent until the first release is published. Absence means never published, not 'unknown'.

release_ids.description: Every published release, oldest first. Append-only.

draft.description: The editable working state. Present from creation; its own fields are all optional.

character-draft.title: CharacterDraft
character-draft.description: The editable working state inside a CharacterCore, and the target of GET/PATCH /v1/characters/{id}. RCE-003. Carries the same authored fields as a release, but every one is optional and age may be unknown or contested: a draft is what exists BEFORE the release constraints can be satisfied. Publishing validates the draft against character-release, which is where the adult-age rule bites (INV-032).

identity.description: Independent of anatomy, orientation, terminology and relationship configuration (INV-014).

attributes.description: Named appearance attributes, each in a FactEnvelope so narration cannot quietly restate one (the eye-color drift counterexample). Locked attributes reject model-derived edits (INV-007).

anatomy.description: Explicit structure overrides on top of the preset pinned in pins.anatomy_preset_release_id. The preset reference lives in exactly one place so a release cannot disagree with its own pin. A structure definition is not evidence of possession (INV-016).

orientation.description: Independent of relationship configuration: monogamy is not a substitute for attraction (INV-014).

terminology.description: Preferred vocabulary maps to canonical structure IDs. Naming a structure does not create it (INV-015).

preferences.description: Boundaries are separate from personality descriptors and are never a consent record. Current willingness is a runtime record, not part of a release (INV-030, INV-033).

agency.description: Player-control permissions (INV-035: fiction never overrides these).

age.description: May be known, unknown or contested while drafting. A release may not be published until this is known and adult.

character-instance.title: CharacterInstance
character-instance.description: A character as it exists inside one scenario continuity. RCE-003. Pins a source release and adds explicit overrides; resolving an instance never writes to the release or the core (INV-012). Memories, beliefs and runtime conditions are NOT here — they are separate continuity-scoped records referencing this instance.

source_release_id.description: Pinned. A newer release of the same core does not retroactively change this instance.

resolved_definition_hash.description: SHA-256 of the resolved view. The same release plus the same overrides must reproduce it (INV-013).

overrides.description: Keyed by path so a path can appear at most once — two conflicting overrides of the same field are unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged. propertyNames enumerates the REAL overridable fields of a release plus dynamic appearance attributes, so a path that does not exist on a release (identity.not_a_field) is rejected rather than validating into something that cannot be deterministically applied. Notably absent are age, id, core_id and owner_id — a scenario override can never move the adult gate or reassign ownership (INV-018, INV-032).

character-preview.title: CharacterPreview
character-preview.description: What the catalog may show about a release to someone who does not own it. RCE-003. Redaction is enforced by construction: the permitted field set is enumerated and additionalProperties is false, so a preview built by copying a release fails validation instead of leaking. Secrets, private facts, internal anatomy detail, secret history and any other user's runtime state have no representable place here (INV-022).

age_years.description: A plain integer, not a FactEnvelope: provenance, authority and lock state are internal and are not published.

character-release.title: CharacterRelease
character-release.description: Immutable published snapshot of a CharacterCore. RCE-003. A core edit produces a new release and never mutates an existing one (INV-009). Runtime conditions and memories are referenced, never embedded: a release does not grow as a scenario is played.

visibility.description: Catalog approval and private ownership are separate concerns.

pins.description: A release must pin the anatomy preset it resolved against; without it, resolution is not reproducible (INV-013).

age.description: A publishable release requires an unambiguously adult, known age (INV-032). A draft core may carry unknown age; a release may not. Adulthood is never inferred from appearance, anatomy, species or archetype name.

identity.description: Independent of anatomy, orientation, terminology and relationship configuration (INV-014).

attributes.description: Named appearance attributes, each in a FactEnvelope so narration cannot quietly restate one (the eye-color drift counterexample). Locked attributes reject model-derived edits (INV-007).

anatomy.description: Explicit structure overrides on top of the preset pinned in pins.anatomy_preset_release_id. The preset reference lives in exactly one place so a release cannot disagree with its own pin. A structure definition is not evidence of possession (INV-016).

orientation.description: Independent of relationship configuration: monogamy is not a substitute for attraction (INV-014).

terminology.description: Preferred vocabulary maps to canonical structure IDs. Naming a structure does not create it (INV-015).

preferences.description: Boundaries are separate from personality descriptors and are never a consent record. Current willingness is a runtime record, not part of a release (INV-030, INV-033).

agency.description: Player-control permissions (INV-035: fiction never overrides these).

common.Utc.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC. A non-UTC offset is rejected.

common.Revision.description: Monotonic per-entity revision used for optimistic concurrency (INV-025).

common.SchemaVersion.description: Semantic version of the schema this record was written against.

common.KnowledgeStatus.description: World-level epistemic state of the record in authoritative storage, NOT any character's belief. 'known': canon records a value. 'unknown': canon records that no value is established. 'contested': two equal-authority facts conflict (INV-006). A character's confidence in a proposition is a separate Belief record (INV-008).

common.Authority.description: Totally ordered, highest first (INV-002). A value may only be replaced by one of equal or higher authority.

common.LockState.description: A lock prevents model-derived edits; it does not prevent an authorized scoped author operation (INV-007).

common.OwnerScope.description: Ownership is a stored edge, never inferred from the payload (INV-018).

common.ContinuityScope.description: Continuity-scoped rows carry their scope explicitly (INV-017, INV-020, INV-021).

common.Extensions.description: Inert namespaced extension data. Never interpreted, always preserved across round-trip and migration. Keys must be 'vendor.name'; unknown fields anywhere else are rejected rather than silently kept.

common.PinnedVersions.description: Pinned, not floating. Resolution of a pinned release is reproducible (INV-013).

fact-envelope.title: FactEnvelope
fact-envelope.description: Wrapper making every authored or derived value auditable. RCE-003. Three states are structurally distinct: an ABSENT envelope means nothing was ever recorded; knowledge_status 'unknown' means canon records that no value is established; 'contested' means equal-authority facts conflict. A null value is never a way to say any of these (INV-005).

value.description: Present only when knowledge_status is 'known'. Null is forbidden; absence of knowledge is expressed by knowledge_status, never by a null.

candidates.description: Present only when knowledge_status is 'contested'. Each conflicting value with its own provenance; none silently wins (INV-006).

gates.GateId.description: account_access: the principal is authenticated, authorized for this resource, AND carries a valid current UserEligibility assurance where adult access is evaluated — all three, failing closed (INV-030). fictional_adult_eligibility: the character's age is known and adult. player_content_authorization: the player's own content opt-in, outside fiction. character_current_willingness: the character's scoped, revocable in-fiction willingness. provider_capability: what the model adapter actually permits.

gates.GateOutcome.description: 'unknown' denies. A gate that cannot be evaluated is never treated as satisfied (INV-005, INV-030).

gates.GateDenialReason.description: Stable reasons, each naming a GATE'S OWN failure mode rather than the circumstance that triggered the check (INV-031). A descriptive fact may trigger revalidation — a location change putting a request outside an affirmed scope, for instance — but the recorded reason is willingness_out_of_scope, never the location. No reason here is, or may become, a descriptive fact about a person, their history, their body, their dispositions or their circumstances: not preference, orientation, tags, traits, reputation, relationship status or history, repeated past action, bodily response, silence, dress or presentation, setting, time of day, world lore, or prior scene content. Those may deny; none may satisfy.

gates.GateReport.description: Every gate is reported exactly once, so a caller can never mistake an unevaluated or duplicated gate for a satisfied one. Constrained by identity rather than by array length: a report with account_access twice and willingness missing is rejected. A report is authoritative only for the moment it was evaluated; willingness in particular is rechecked at execution and at commit (INV-033).

permitted.description: Derived, not asserted: true requires every outcome to be satisfied, false requires at least one that is not. Never a substitute for reading the individual outcomes.

persona.title: Persona
persona.description: The user's fictional identity inside a scenario. RCE-003. This is NOT the user's real identity record: no legal name, no contact details, no assurance evidence, no document reference may appear here. Real-user eligibility lives on UserAccount and is a separate check from fictional adulthood (INV-030).

age.description: Explicit fictional adult age. Same rule as a release: known and adult, never inferred (INV-032).

resolved-character.title: ResolvedCharacter
resolved-character.description: The computed view an instance presents to the engine: preset and archetype defaults, then explicit core values, then authorized scenario overrides (INV-010). Derived and never stored as truth — it is reproducible from its inputs, which is what resolution_hash asserts. RCE-055 owns the resolution algorithm; this schema fixes only the shape of its output.

inputs.description: Everything that determined this view. Resolution is reproducible only if all of it is pinned.

fields.description: Resolved values keyed by dotted path. Each records which layer supplied it, so a reviewer can see why a value is what it is and no layer's contribution is anonymous.

supplied_by.description: Which layer won for this field.

unresolved.description: Paths that could not be resolved. Present so an engine reads 'unresolved' rather than inventing confirmation (INV-016).

sse-event.title: Conversation SSE events
sse-event.description: The five event types on GET /v1/conversations/{id}/events, per API.md. RCE-053. Every event carries a durable id scoped to the conversation and branch, so Last-Event-ID resumes deterministically. No unvalidated model token event exists in v1: a client that receives turn.committed is receiving already-canon output (ADR-005, INV-028).

id.description: Durable sequence scoped to conversation and branch. Monotonic within that scope, not globally.

data.description: Carries the committed result only: turn, resulting scene revision, message ids and the validated utterances.
Sent when a Last-Event-ID cursor has expired. Instructs a bounded canonical fetch rather than replaying unbounded history.

turn.TurnState.description: committed, failed and cancelled are terminal. A model refusal is a failed turn outcome, never an HTTP auth error.

turn.UtteranceKind.description: A narrator utterance declares itself rather than impersonating a player (API.md). There is no 'player' kind: player input is durable input, not generated output.

client_message_id.description: Client-durable uniqueness that outlives idempotency-key retention, so a retry cannot duplicate chat input.

text.description: Baseline cap. maxLength bounds CHARACTERS; the 16 KiB UTF-8 byte limit from API.md is a separate check and is the binding one for multibyte text.

addressee_instance_ids.description: At most four AI-controlled instances per conversation (ADR-001).

turn.TurnView.description: The durable, pollable state of a turn. Carries no unvalidated model output in v1 (ADR-005).

turn.ActionProposal.description: A proposed change to physical or relational state. Always a proposal: it carries evidence, never authority (INV-004).

turn.Claim.description: An assertion extracted from generated text. Authority is always 'derived' here — an extractor cannot mint canon (INV-004).

turn.ValidationResult.description: Per DOMAIN.md. A rejected candidate never becomes accepted history (INV-028).

invariant.description: The invariant this issue violates, where one applies. Cited rather than restated.

turn.ActionBatchRequest.description: A dry-run batch. The snapshot revision is required because validation is meaningless without the state it was evaluated against (API.md).

actions.description: Ordered. Order is significant: simultaneous actions are validated against intermediate state.

turn.ActionValidationResponse.description: A validation outcome, plus the token that authorizes a later commit of the same payload. The token binds payload hash, principal, policy revision and snapshot (API.md), so it is issued only when the outcome is valid.

turn.ActionCommitRequest.description: Commit of a previously validated batch. The actions are resent so the token can bind their payload hash, and expected_scene_revision is rechecked against current state at commit (ADR-004, INV-025).

actions.description: Ordered. Order is significant: simultaneous actions are validated against intermediate state.

sessionCookie.name: rce_session
sessionCookie.description: Opaque Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Lax session cookie. CSRF protection applies on unsafe methods.

adminRole.name: rce_session
adminRole.description: The same session, additionally carrying an administration role granted by trusted administration only.

deletionReceipt.name: X-Deletion-Receipt
deletionReceipt.description: Narrowly scoped expiring receipt from account erasure. Grants status reads only, after the session it replaced was revoked.
